headline: P-16 NIR power transfer FEASIBLE under corrected diffuse transmittance model. Initial ballistic model was WRONG (model error, not mechanism failure — Article XXIX). At 940nm with 1cm² PV receiver through human scalp+skull (1.5cm total): 744 μW electrical output — 7.4x margin over 100 μW duty-cycled requirement, 149x over 5 μW pacemaker-grade. P-16 TEV upgraded from $29K to $57K (P_tech 0.25→0.45). P-16 invention thesis defined: external NIR → diffuse transcranial transmittance → implant PV → adaptive energy management → zero-battery chronic sensing. P-15 vs P-16 comparison: complementary (P-15 autonomous low-power, P-16 externally powered high-power). Prior art: subcutaneous NIR PV exists (LITERATURE_VERIFIED), mouse transcranial demonstrated (Nature Biotech 2025), but human-scale chronic transcranial NIR for therapeutic implant NOT demonstrated. P-16's contribution: human-scale feasibility + adaptive energy management + clinical integration.

P0_P16_power_model.critical_correction: Initial ballistic Beer-Lambert model gave ZERO power (model error — total scattering coefficient 150-200 cm⁻¹ makes exp(-300) ≈ 0). Corrected to diffuse transmittance model using mu_eff = sqrt(3*mu_a*(mu_a+mu_s')) with reduced scattering mu_s' = mu_s*(1-g), g=0.9. This accounts for scattered photons reaching detector.
P0_P16_power_model.result: At 940nm, T_total = 2.66% through scalp+skull. With 1cm² GaAs PV (28% eff) at 100 mW/cm² safety limit: 744 μW. FEASIBLE for all power budgets (5/25/100 μW).

P1_prior_art.strongest_argument: Subcutaneous NIR PV demonstrated (PubMed 29056754: 17% Si, 31% GaAs at 850nm). Mouse transcranial demonstrated (Nature Biotech 2025). But human-scale chronic transcranial NIR through 10mm skull at safe illumination for therapeutic implant NOT demonstrated. P-16's contribution: human-scale feasibility + adaptive energy management + clinical integration.
P1_prior_art.potentially_novel: Human-scale transcranial NIR power delivery + adaptive energy management for fluctuating optical power + zero-battery chronic therapeutic sensing through skull

P2_invention_thesis.input: External NIR (940nm or 1064nm) at safety-limited irradiance
P2_invention_thesis.transformation: Diffuse transmittance through scalp(0.5cm)+skull(1.0cm) → implantable PV
P2_invention_thesis.control_law: Adaptive energy management: sensing duty cycle dynamically adapts to fluctuating transcranial optical power
P2_invention_thesis.unexpected_benefit: Zero-battery chronic implantable sensing through intact skull. No replacement surgery. Wearable NIR patch for home use.

P3_P15_vs_P16.verdict: COMPLEMENTARY, NOT duplicates. P-15: autonomous, low-power (1-10μW), zero patient effort. P-16: externally powered, high-power (744+μW), requires NIR patch. Different use cases.
P3_P15_vs_P16.winner_by_dimension: P-16 wins on energy density (74x), burst power, implant simplicity. P-15 wins on autonomy, patient dependence, thermal, workflow.
